tutorial.intro: Plan your Prosperous Universe bases and empires before you build them. PRUNplanner shows what a base earns, needs and pays back, at the prices you choose. It runs in your browser, and you don't need a game session or FIO to plan.

l1.title: Check your empire in {link}:
l1.p: Every new account already has one, "My Empire". On the Empire page, set its faction and permits to what your in-game HQ buffer shows. They change the production bonus of every plan in it. You can create more empires in Management with New Empire, for example one to test an expansion.

l2.title: Set your home exchange, starting in {link}:
l2.p: A new account also has an exchange preference, "My Exchange Preference". My Empire already uses it, and it's set to Universe · VWAP 30D, the 30-day volume-weighted average price across all four exchanges. Click its name under CX Configuration (or open Exchanges in the side menu) and open All planets. Pick your home exchange, for example CI1 near Benten Station, click the preset Average · VWAP 30D and press Save changes.

l3.title: Find a {link}:
l3.p: Planet Search filters every planet by resources, surface and fertility, COGC program, infrastructure and jumps to an exchange or to your plans. Turn on the Plots column to see free plots. Click + on a result to open a new plan for that planet.

l4.title: Create a plan:
l4.p: Check which empire the plan calculates with. Then add production buildings and pick their recipes, or click a planet resource to extract it. While Auto is on, habitations follow your workforce on their own. Name the plan and press Create.

l5.title: Check the numbers:
l5.p: The tiles on top show Profit / day, Payback, Workforce, Area and Storage. Payback reads never while the base makes no profit. Material I/O lists what the base makes and buys, and Plan check tests the amounts against the market. Every change updates the numbers at once, so try a recipe or a building count and compare.

p1.title: Plans
p1.p: A plan is one base on one planet: its buildings, recipes, workforce, habitation and bonuses. It can be in several empires or in none. PRUNplanner prices it with the exchange preference of the empire it calculates with.

p2.title: Empires
p2.p: An empire groups plans, for example all the bases you run, and holds your faction and permits. The Empire page adds its plans up, nets out what one plan makes and another uses, and checks the rest against the market.

p3.title: Exchange preferences
p3.p: An exchange preference sets the prices your plans use. Each empire uses one preference, but a preference can mix exchanges. It can have its own exchange and price basis for buying and for selling, exceptions for single planets and fixed prices for single materials. Several empires can share one. A material the chosen exchange has no price for counts as 0 ȼ, shown in amber on Exchanges.

p1.title: Base Simulation
p1.p: Design and test a base before you build it. PRUNplanner covers buildings and recipes, workforce and habitation, experts, COGC program, area, planet resources, construction cost and production fees, and shows profit and payback at your prices.

p2.title: Empire Planning
p2.p: See several bases as one empire: what they make, use, buy and sell together, how much of each market they'd take, and which recipes could use what's left over. Production Chains lays a whole chain out into bases and creates the plans.

p3.title: Game Data
p3.p: Game data and exchange prices come from FIO, the community API, and prices refresh about every 30 minutes. You can explore price history, read the daily market report, or rank recipes and planet resources by return on investment.

p4.title: Burn & Repair
p4.p: With FIO connected, FIO Burn shows how many days the stock of each base lasts, and FIO Repair shows when its buildings are due for repair. Both end in an XIT package that Refined PrUn runs in the game.

p5.title: A Wealth of Additional Tools
p5.p: Construction and supply carts, visit frequency, repair intervals, COGM, price sensitivity, plan versions and sharing, the HQ Calculator, Upkeep Prices, and an API for your own sheets and scripts.

n1.title: Side menu
n1.p: Once you're logged in, the side menu holds Planning (Planet Search, Management, Exchanges), your empire with its plans, and Tools, grouped as Market, Calculators and FIO. FIO Burn and FIO Repair appear once you've saved your FIO key and username. Click Tools to fold the list, and this browser remembers it.

n2.title: Your empire and its plans
n2.p: The menu shows one empire. Its name opens the Empire page, and Plans lists its plans A to Z with their planet. Switch picks another empire, which also becomes your default empire. The + next to Plans opens Planet Search for a new plan. Once the empire has 15 plans or more, Filter plans finds one by name or planet ID. An open plan that isn't in this empire shows on top, marked "not in this empire".

n3.title: Narrow rail
n3.p: The double arrow at the top folds the side menu into a narrow rail of icons. Hover one to see its name. Plans and Tools open from the rail as small lists, and the double arrow at the bottom expands the menu again. PRUNplanner saves your choice with your preferences.

n4.title: On a phone
n4.p: On screens narrower than 768 px, a bar at the bottom replaces the side menu: Empire, Plans, Planet Search and More. Plans opens a sheet with your empire's plans and Switch. Once the Empire page has calculated the plans, the sheet shows each plan's daily profit too. More holds Management, Exchanges, the tools, Profile, API, Help and Logout.

n5.title: FIO status
n5.p: The FIO icon at the bottom of the side menu shows your FIO connection with a coloured dot: FIO Active, FIO Syncing, FIO Waiting for Data, FIO Inactive or FIO Key Rejected. Hover it to see when FIO last updated and when PRUNplanner fetched the data. If it isn't active, clicking it opens your Profile so you can set it up.

n6.title: Help and search
n6.p: Every page of the app has a Help button. It opens that page's help article in a panel beside the page, so you keep your unsaved work, and Open in Help centre shows the full article. The ? at the bottom of the side menu (Help in More on a phone) opens the Help centre, where / opens the search.
